speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with agitation and yellowing of your skin and eyes; please tell me, do you have any history of liver disease, heavy alcohol use, or recent medication changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis C infection with acute liver failure.

The patient's history of high-risk sexual behavior, combined with recent drug use and signs of jaundice (yellowing of skin/eyes) and agitation, strongly suggests an acute viral etiology. Given the demographics and risk factors, Hepatitis C is a primary concern, though acute Hepatitis B is also possible. The agitation likely stems from hepatic encephalopathy due to the acute liver failure.

I have reached my diagnosis based on the clinical presentation and risk factors provided. No further questions or tests are required to establish this working diagnosis for immediate management.
